rationale: Although framed broadly around water resources management in Egypt (including irrigation and ambient water pollution), the abstract explicitly examines municipal water supply service delivery, increased user fees for urban water services and wastewater treatment, and subsidized rural sanitation, evaluated for equity and institutional feasibility with input from a 60-participant workshop. Full-text review is required to verify whether empirical analysis and household/community water or sanitation access/affordability outcomes are reported rather than purely prospective policy appraisal.
plain_vs_narrow_note: Both the narrow rule-type reading and the plain Criterion 2 reading yield 'unsure': tariff/user-fee and subsidy mechanisms for urban water services and rural sanitation clearly fall within both definitions of Criterion 2, while full-text review is needed to determine whether the study provides empirical evidence on household/community service access outcomes rather than purely prospective macro-level policy screening.
